canonical_statement: The study asks whether a reference-free LLM judge can be screened before deployment to determine whether its scores discriminate verifier-correct from verifier-incorrect answers during text-space skill optimization.

The reference-free judge is modeled as a latent solver with competence c: it implicitly re-solves the item, disperses errors across the remaining k-1 answers, and scores consistency between the candidate answer and its internal solution.
Under assumptions A1-A3, the paper derives AUC = 1/2 + (ck-1)/(2(k-1)) for answer-level judge discriminability.
Competence above the answer-space chance floor, c > 1/k, is a necessary but not sufficient condition for above-chance reference-free judge discriminability.
In the free-text limit k→∞, the model gives AUC=(1+c)/2, so competence contributes more directly to discriminability because independent errors are unlikely to coincide verbatim.
The paper defines a within-question AUC that pairs positive and negative episodes only within the same item, making the estimator invariant to additive item-difficulty score components.
A non-intervening probe records judge scores on genuine verifier-controlled optimization episodes while leaving accept/reject decisions unchanged.
Discriminability confidence intervals use a question-clustered bootstrap because episodes are clustered within items.
The judge probe feeds answer content rather than only a multiple-choice letter because a content-free feed can force AUC to chance independently of judge competence.
Closed-book competence uses empty-inclusive accuracy: non-convergent or unparsable generations within the budget are counted as unsolved rather than dropped.

Benchmark-exposure inflation is estimated with a domain- and difficulty-matched, less-exposed proxy benchmark and compared with a grading-only AUC-inversion competence estimate that has different error sources.
The AUC-inversion competence estimate is c_hat=[(k-1)(2*AUC-1)+1]/k, reducing to 2*AUC-1 in the free-text limit.
Primary experiments use SkillOpt, Haiku as the target model, and Claude Sonnet as the judge on research mathematics, factual QA, and GPQA-Diamond with 210, 360, and 198 episodes respectively.
Cross-provider replication evaluates DeepSeek-8B, Qwen-7B, Xiaomi MiMo-7B, and DeepSeek-V4-flash through the same harness with a matched 16k-token budget.

The closed-loop pilot compares verifier, judge, and random acceptance gates while holding target and optimizer models fixed; verifier scores are retained only for offline evaluation in judge and random arms.
The diagnostic is evaluated only on objectively checkable single-answer tasks with gold answers and verifier labels; genuinely open-ended rubric-based judging is left for future work.

The latent-solver assumption is scoped to single-answer tasks judged without rubrics or external evidence and may understate judges when verification has solution-independent standards or cheap local checks.
GPQA-Diamond is evaluated in a single pass and therefore has no within-question strata, so only an optimistic marginal AUC can be reported for that task.
Closed-book self-solve competence may lower-bound grading-context competence because seeing a candidate answer and reasoning can scaffold re-solving.
The less-exposed proxy benchmark is domain- and difficulty-matched but is not the same instrument as GPQA-Diamond, so part of the estimated exposure gap may reflect dataset mismatch.

canonical_statement: The cross-provider matrix reports marginal AUC because per-episode judge scores were not retained, leaving factual-QA results exposed to the difficulty confound.
The closed-loop pilot uses only three seeds for factual QA and two for mathematics, supporting ordering and error-type claims rather than precise effect-size estimates.
The study does not establish whether a judge that passes the screen remains safe under sustained optimization, distribution drift, or Goodhart pressure.

canonical_statement: In the factual-QA pilot, the judge that passed the screen admitted no harmful candidates and made one-sided errors by over-rejecting improvements (false-reject rate 0.44).

source_anchor.paragraph: Passing the screen avoids harmful acceptance in this pilot

canonical_statement: The authors recommend estimating uncontaminated judge competence on the target task before deployment and declining judge gating when competence does not clear the task chance floor.
The authors conclude that genuine task competence, rather than headline benchmark accuracy, is the relevant input for deciding whether a reference-free judge can supply discriminative gate signal.
